label: Fields and dotted paths
gloss: a field name reads a value off the record; a dotted path reads inside a nested object, like po.poTotal
why: Records nest. A lookup attaches a whole row under one name (po), and a source can carry an object (vendor) inside the record. A dotted path walks into those: po.poTotal is the poTotal field of the po object; vendor.id is the id inside vendor. Every tool has a way to say this, and getting the path wrong is the most common reason an expression comes back null.
cue: when an expression is null, check the path step by step: does po exist, and does it have poTotal with that exact spelling
task: Read into the nested parts of the record: set variance to invoiceTotal minus the PO total, and vendorMatch to whether the vendor id on the invoice equals the vendor id on the PO.
notes: invoiceTotal is a top-level field; po.poTotal reads poTotal inside the po object the lookup attached.
vendor.id reads id inside the vendor object that arrived with the invoice.
Spelling and case matter: po.PoTotal is a different (missing) path.

checks.label: INV-1 vendorMatch is true (vendor.id equals po.vendorId)
